content: Sodium thiocyanate is a chemical compound with the molecular formula NaSCN. It is a colorless, deliquescent salt and serves as one of the primary sources of the thiocyanate anion. Due to this property, it is widely utilized as a precursor in the synthesis of pharmaceuticals and other specialty chemicals. Thiocyanate salts, including sodium thiocyanate, are typically synthesized through the reaction of cyanide with elemental sulfur. Sodium thiocyanate crystallizes in an orthorhombic lattice structure. In this structure, each sodium ion (Na⁺) is coordinated by three sulfur atoms and three nitrogen atoms, which are provided by the triatomic thiocyanate anion. Applications in Chemical Synthesis Sodium thiocyanate (NaSCN) is commonly used to convert alkyl halides into their corresponding alkyl thiocyanates. Related reagents, such as ammonium thiocyanate and potassium thiocyanate, are also employed in similar reactions. Notably, potassium thiocyanate exhibits twice the solubility in water compared to sodium thiocyanate. In situ generation of reactive species from NaSCN is a common practice. For example, sodium thiocyanate can react with organic amines to produce derivatives of thiourea.
